Products have not had to travel as far.

The Romans invaded in {AD 43} and stayed for about {400} years.
In {1066} William of {Normandy} defeated Harold at the Battle of {Hastings}.
The {Black Death} of 1348 killed one {third} of England’s population.
King {John} was forced to agree to the {Magna Carta} in 1215.
The Wars of the Roses ended at {Bosworth Field} in {{#}}.
Henry VIII founded the {Church of England} and married {six} times.
The Spanish Armada was defeated in {1588}, in the reign of {Elizabeth I}.
The {Habeas Corpus} Act of 1679 means no one can be {held prisoner unlawfully}.
The Act of Union of {1707} created the Kingdom of {Great Britain}.
The first Prime Minister was Sir Robert {Walpole}, whilst George {I} was king.
Bonnie Prince Charlie was defeated at {Culloden} in {{#}}.
The slave trade was abolished in {1807} and slavery in the Empire in {1833}.
Admiral {Nelson} won at Trafalgar; the Duke of {Wellington} beat Napoleon at Waterloo.
Queen Victoria came to the throne in {1837} at the age of {18}.
The {Chartists} campaigned for votes for working men; the {suffragettes} for votes for women.
Women over {30} got the vote in 1918; the voting age became {18} in 1969.
The First World War ended at {#}am on {{#} November} {{#}}.
In {#} more than {{#},{#}} men were rescued from {Dunkirk}.
The {NHS} was founded in {#}, led by {Aneurin Bevan}.
The UK joined the EEC in {1973} and left the EU on 31 January {2020}.
The Scottish Parliament has {129} members and the Northern Ireland Assembly has {90}.
A jury has {12} members in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and {15} in Scotland.
Small claims are under {£10,000} in England and Wales, and under {£5,000} in Scotland and Northern Ireland.
The patron saint of Wales is St {David}, whose day is {1 March}.
The Prime Minister lives at {10 Downing Street} and has a country house called {Chequers}.
You must be {{#}} to drive a car and {{#}} to ride a moped.
{Sir Tim Berners-Lee} invented the World Wide Web and {Alan Turing} the Turing machine.
The {Proms} are organised by the BBC, with the last night at the {Royal Albert Hall}.
The {Turner Prize} is for contemporary art; the {Man Booker Prize} is for fiction.
Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament and the only {Grand Slam} played on {grass}.
Members of the {House of Commons} are elected, whilst members of the {House of Lords} are not.
The Isle of Man is a Crown dependency, not part of the UK.
The Falklands are an overseas territory; the others are Crown dependencies.
St Augustine was the first Archbishop of Canterbury, not a patron saint.
The poppy is worn for Remembrance; the others are national flowers.
Trafalgar was a sea battle; the others were fought on land.
Mary, Queen of Scots was not one of Henry VIII’s wives.
Mary I was a Catholic; the others were Protestant.
Dickens was a novelist; the others were inventors.
Constable was a painter; the others were composers.
Henry Moore was a sculptor; the others were novelists.
Lent is Christian; the others are festivals of other faiths.
Westminster is the UK Parliament; the others are devolved.
